To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) cooperation is explained by a process of cultural evolution, and (b) the process of cultural evolution is explained by the internalization of altruistic norms.

(a) the capacity to internalize social norms is the key to understanding prosocial behavior, and (b) the capacity to develop internalized norms is a biological adaptation that has evolved through cultural evolution.

cooperation can be explained in a unified way by a bioeconomic model of cultural evolution that combines the sociological concept internalization, the biological concepts of cultural and biological transmission, and the economic concepts of replicator dynamics and the rational actor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution of cooperation.
how and why humans cooperate.
how and why people cooperate with one another and with how cooperation is maintained.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the puzzle of prosociality is solved.

we have shown that the human capacity for cooperation and prosociality is an evolved adaptation, but one that has been shaped in a particular way, by the interaction of biological and cultural evolution, in which biological evolution shaped the human brain to be a powerful learning device, and cultural evolution has used that capacity to shape the norms of cooperation and prosocial behavior.
the puzzle of prosociality has been solved.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the puzzle of prosociality can only be solved if we combine sociological, biological and economic insights.

we have developed a model of human behavior which is consistent with the biological fact that we are a species of primates, the sociological fact that we are social animals, and the economic fact that we are rational actors.
we are able to explain the emergence of cooperation among unrelated individuals by the interaction of three factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can solve the puzzle of prosociality by combining the central contributions of sociology, biology, and economics.
the internalization of prosocial norms is the key to explaining human cooperation.
the puzzle of prosociality can be solved by a synthesis of sociological, biological, and economic insights.
